text:
alex: Heads-up — hit an odd path in staging: when a private tenant falls back to hosted, the request sometimes loses the probe header and we drop to authz-fail -> fallback model. Repro steps in thread.

mika: ugh, is this the probe-less switch we discussed last week?

alex: yeah. root cause looks like the local probe agent strips x-infer-probe on sidecarless transitions. observed on 2 runs.

cheng: can you paste the exact header snapshot? might be a routing rewrite bug.

alex: pasted below:

```
POST /v1/generate
Host: infer.redwood.internal
Authorization: Bearer redacted
x-tenant-id: tenant-42
x-infer-probe: lease=abc123;mode=probe
```

After pass-through to hosted controlplane:

```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: Bearer redacted
x-tenant-id: tenant-42
# missing x-infer-probe
```

samira: so hosted sees no probe and applies default authz policy -> counts as public request and triggers the fallback model. That explains the regression in quality.

leo: what's the minimal fix? re-add header in proxy or make hosted accept a probe token in body?

nora: re-adding header in the proxy seems simplest but risky: it requires trust that the sidecar didn't intentionally drop it. Could be exploited if we gratuitously trust a header from the edge.

mika: agreed. security concern. Alternative: propagate a signed probe assertion via a short-lived JWT that the controlplane verifies with our KMS.

cheng: signed assertion would be safer but needs KMS glue in private deployments. Private customers may be air-gapped; they may not want our KMS calls.

alex: exactly. Private setups often use customer-managed KMS/HSM. We could require the sidecar to sign with local key and the hosted controlplane to verify with an admission cert — but that means a trust anchor exchange during handshake.

samira: that's more plumbing. Another option: when falling back, the local controlplane passes a one-time bearer (probe token) in the request body: {"probe_token":"<opaque>"}. Hosted controlplane validates against cache of issued tokens via our federation channel.

leo: federation channel? that implies connectivity between private controlplane and hosted verification endpoint. Some private customers block outbound to our domains.

nora: true. We need a pattern that supports three classes: fully-connected private, proxy-only private (limited egress), and air-gapped. Any solution must degrade gracefully.

mika: proposal: layered approach
1) Preferred: signed probe assertion (JWT signed by customer's KMS) verified by hosted using exchanged certs during onboarding.
2) Fallback: short-lived opaque probe tokens synced over optional federation (if allowed).
3) Lowest: revert to header re-injection only for customers who explicitly opt-in (consent + risk acceptance).

alex: that covers trade-offs. Implementation notes:
- Add handshake field: "probe_trust: [signed,jwt],[opaque],[header_optin]"
- Require manifest flag for opt-in behaviors
- Add audit log entry when header-reinjection is used :eyes:

cheng: how about runtime perf? signing per-request adds latency. We should support signing once per probe lease and reuse the assertion for the lease lifetime.

samira: yes -- assertions should be lease-scoped and cached. We already have lease IDs in the KV cache logic; piggyback that.

leo: are there any model-serving implications? If fallbacks are frequent, we might see higher cost due to hosted model use. We should emit a metric: fallback_reason=probe-loss vs capacity.

nora: +1 to metrics. We also need SLO docs update: explain which tenants might see fidelity gaps during mode transitions.

alex: action items:
- cheng: draft handshake manifest change and cert exchange flow (ETA 2d)
- mika: security review on signed assertion + KMS patterns (ETA 3d)
- samira: add metric/fallback_reason and audit log schema (ETA 2d)
- leo: patch proxy to preserve probe header for opt-in customers (small PR)

ops-bot: deploy-check: staging cluster tests queued (job/handshake-probe-check v1) :white_check_mark:

mika: one more UX thing — console should surface "probe trust mode" per tenant and show when fallback occurred and why.

alex: yup. I'll add a console ticket.

cheng: tiny nit: ensure the manifest change is backward compatible. If hosted sees no handshake info, assume header_optin=false (secure default).

samira: +1. Secure default.

leo: I'll open the proxy PR and add integration test that simulates sidecarless handoff.

nora: let's sync tomorrow 11am to review the handshake draft. Put on my calendar.

alex: thanks everyone. filing RFC follow-up with notes and linking this thread. :sparkles:
